summary: Standing 1955 L-4 lookout cab on a 30-foot tower on Poker Jim Butte in the Custer Gallatin forest, NRHP-listed 2022, with a drive-up road.

facts.design: L-4 pattern lookout cab (14 by 14 ft) on a 30-foot timber tower

access.note: A road runs to the top of the butte beside the Poker Jim Picnic Ground. No source says whether the cab is open to visitors.

events.note: First lookout on the summit; the NRHP nomination puts a lookout there by spring 1936. Other sources give 1935 or 1937.
A lookout and his wife stationed on the peak all summer; register recorded 186 tourists from 19 states
Original lookout removed and replaced by the present L-4 cab on a 30-foot tower
Present L-4 cab built on a 30-foot tower
Blazes in the Ashland and Fort Howes districts; the lookout tower was evacuated
Stairs, rails, catwalk deck and floor joists replaced to address safety problems
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places September 1, 2022

corrections.why: NHLR and FirelookOut both describe a 30-foot tower, and the nomination says 'thirty-foot tall three-bay tower'. The record's 6.1 m (20 ft) matches the earlier 1937 pole tower, not the present 1955 structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination says a lookout was present by spring 1936 and once dates the original to 1935. A September 1937 newspaper says the tower was built 'last spring' (1936). NHLR and FirelookOut give 1937. The story gives the range rather than picking one.

The 2022 Forest Service nomination says the lookout is staffed through summer and fall; FirelookOut says it is used during emergencies. The story reports both. The facts use the nomination, a formal federal document.
NHLR and FirelookOut give 4,325 ft (1,318 m); the Forest Service page and nomination give 4,348 ft. The record keeps 1,318.3 m from NHLR.

notes_for_editor: The original lookout's date is not settled (1935, 1936 or 1937 across sources), so the story gives the range. The NRHP nomination is the strongest source for the current structure and the 2008 work. An Independent Press article (which a search snippet says gives 1939) returned HTTP 429 twice and was not used. The 1937 and 1966 facts come from newspaper quotes reproduced on a hobbyist site, not the original papers. The access level is unknown: the picnic ground and road are public, but no source says whether the cab itself is open to visitors. Height correction (6.1 m to 9.1 m) is the main fix to the record. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the forest name is now sourced to the NRHP form; the 1937 last spring wording and the 1966 Ashland and Fort Howes blazes have exact evidence quotes; the story's causal link between the 1966 blazes and the evacuation was removed; and the sentence saying the cab had stood in its 1955 form since the 2008 repairs was dropped as unsupported.
